title: On Kicking the ball past three boys
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：kick　|　正文 354 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 kick 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the warden ① kicked the ball past three boys year after year, and every resident in the centre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the warden ② kicks the ball past three boys for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ kick the ball past three boys at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ kicked the ball past three boys before — a line in the register for June 1946 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Kicking the ball past three boys year after year, the warden said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the notice at the far gate, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ kick the door open with one boot for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Kick the door open with one boot at once and never mention it again.

By 1959 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the register, and a new resident from the next centre ⑧ kicks the door open with one boot year after year every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the gate, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ kicked the ball past three boys again when nobody else would.

⑩ To kick the ball past three boys, my mother said in 1964, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the centre remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the centre forgets, somebody kicks the ball past three boys for the whole place again and somebody must kick the ball past three boys year after year all over again.

task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 踢（一般过去式 kicked the ball past three boys：1952 年管理员头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 踢（一般现在 kicks the ball past three boys：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 踢（不定式 to kick the ball past three boys：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 踢（过去完成时 had kicked the ball past three boys：1946 年六月的登记册上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 踢（动名词 kicking the ball past three boys 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 踢掉（kick the door open with one boot：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去踢掉一脚把门踢开）
G. v. 踢掉（kick the door open with one boot：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 踢（后段两处：新来的居民照例 kicks the door open with one boot，而母亲又一次 kicked the ball past three boys）

answers.why: kick 意为“踢”，1952 年管理员年年地踢把球从三个男孩身边踢过，那是社区中心里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 kicked。
kick 意为“踢”，自那以后管理员替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 kicks。
kick 意为“踢”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯踢把球从三个男孩身边踢过”，此处为不定式 to kick the ball past three boys。
kick 意为“踢”，登记册里 六月 那行字说明早在 1959 年之前就有人踢过，故用过去完成时 had kicked。
kick 意为“踢”，管理员说“踢把球从三个男孩身边踢过这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 kicking the ball past three boys 作主语。
kick 意为“踢掉”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去踢掉一脚把门踢开”，should ever 之后用原形 kick the door open with one boot。
kick 意为“踢掉”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻踢掉一脚把门踢开（kick the door open with one boot at once），以后再也不要提起。
kick 意为“踢”，新来的居民每个月份都照例踢掉一脚把门踢开，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 kicks。
kick 意为“踢”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次年年地踢把球从三个男孩身边踢过，用一般过去式 kicked 叙述。
kick 意为“踢”，结尾那句是母亲 1964 年的话：要踢把球从三个男孩身边踢过，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和社区中心记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 kick 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1952 the warden kicked the ball past three boys year after year, and nobody in the centre forgot it.
Even now the warden kicks the ball past three boys for the whole place whenever the centre asks.
Kicking the ball past three boys year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever kick the door open with one boot for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new resident from the next centre kicks the door open with one boot year after year every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother kicked the ball past three boys again, and the centre remembered that half.
